text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000009 bills 99215 well above expectation at every complexity level, but the few charts returned support the billed codes, so the pattern cannot yet be resolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 share is not confined to sicker patients: it runs several times the all-provider rate in every complexity stratum, including patients with 0 or 1 conditions, so panel acuity alone does not appear to explain it. The records review points the other way. None of the documented claims at any level fell below the billed level, but only 6 documented 99215 claims came back, which is too thin to clear the provider. Some signs suggest the notes may not reflect what happened, though none is proof: the note problem rate, repeated visit times, and the 3 claims documenting moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line. C0004639 stands out: it is a single-condition hyperlipidemia visit billed 99215, documented as high MDM and flagged as a late note. A reviewer should first obtain charts and the audit trail for the low-complexity 99215 sample (e.g., C0004639, C0004380, C0004529, C0004477) to check whether high MDM is plausible for those encounters, and look for cloned or templated content."}
